rows.10:1e8c:
Haven't you ever been holding a needle or something and thought, 'It would really hurt if I jabbed this under my fingernail'?
When you're deep-frying something, haven't you ever thought, 'What would happen if I plunged my hand into this oil'?
Don't people have moments when they just can't help tormenting themselves?
And then they imagine it actually happening and get a little shiver of excitement.
I do that sort of thing, you know.{p}What about you? Don't you?
rows.10:2120:
So the boy who got curious about the school roof... maybe he just happened to have those self-destructive moments one after another, don't you think?
The boy's name was Nobuhiko Aizawa.
From what I hear, he was a truly ordinary person in every way.
That's exactly why I think so.
"Hey, if you jumped off the roof of this building, do you think you'd survive?"
"Nobuhiko. Have you gone screwy in the head or something?
Where'd that come from all of a sudden?"
When he asked his friends about it, that's what they said, and they laughed at him.
The more seriously Aizawa said it, the funnier his friends thought the joke was, and they laughed even harder.
Aizawa was an ordinary person, after all.
He didn't press them any further; when his friends laughed, he laughed right along with them.{p}
rows.10:23d8:
Even so, whenever he was alone, he agonized over it.
He didn't know why it bothered him so much, and he even wondered whether he himself had gone strange.
Still, the only way to settle it was to actually find out.
Jump himself...
Or push somebody else off.
Every time the thought came to him, he told himself he mustn't think such stupid things. But the harder you hold back, the less you can contain a desire.
And the stronger the desire, the truer that is.
As day followed day, the desire grew with them, and it was only a matter of time before it broke through the shell of reason that held it down.{p}
rows.10:2b58:
He hurriedly worked out a plan and put it into action right away.
He was dying to carry it out as soon as he possibly could.
Luring a delinquent out was easy.
He said there was a guy he wanted roughed up, and he'd pay for it.
Kuwahata took the bait immediately.
...Never dreaming that he would soon be pushed off the roof.
Then, when Kuwahata came up to the roof, Aizawa watched for an opening and made him breathe in the chloroform he had prepared in advance.
Kuwahata went limp at once, before he could even struggle.{p}
rows.10:2d20:
Trembling with excitement that his wish would soon come true, Aizawa dragged Kuwahata's body across the roof to the edge.
There was a railing around the roof, but it wasn't very high.{p}
rows.10:2de0:
Then he hoisted Kuwahata onto his shoulder, leaned out over the railing, and peered down.
It was only a little over ten meters above the ground, but it still made his head spin.
Now that he was actually facing it, Aizawa felt a moment of hesitation.{p}Was it really all right to go through with this?
rows.10:4444:
When he happened to look down, the earth was beckoning to him.
He even had the illusion that it was opening its huge mouth wide, waiting for its prey to fall.
After all, the soil down there had sucked up the blood of three people.
It would be no wonder at all if it had acquired a taste for blood.
Aizawa put his hand on the railing.{p}Then he leaned out even further and stared at the waiting ground.
rows.10:33bc:
The next day at school, everyone was talking about Kuwahata.
His death had been settled as a suicide.
Kuwahata had always been a problem student, so no one looked too deeply into the cause.
For a while after that, Aizawa got to enjoy a wonderfully carefree school life.
...But it lasted only a short time.
As time went on, a problem cropped up again.{p}
rows.10:36b8:
The next day, the second experiment was carried out.
This time, he called out a delinquent, hit him from behind with a bat, and pushed him off while he was weakened.
"...Just as I thought.
Dead again."
This time the head had split open and its contents had spilled out; one look was enough to tell he was dead.{p}
rows.10:3f28:
Aizawa stuffed the guinea pig into a burlap sack he had prepared in advance and carried it on his back to the school.
Then he snuck into the school at night and silently made his way up to the roof.
Of course, the door was locked.
He broke the lock with pliers and a hammer, and the wind came gusting in and struck him full force.{p}
rows.10:4dc0:
Well then, let's go.
...I do think the story that a monster lives in this school is true.
I can't shake the feeling, myself, of being possessed by something.
No, I don't mean me.
I mean all of you at this school.
Though I suppose that includes me, too.{p}
rows.10:5214:
"So if I say it, I'll get to meet him?"
{f:I|I} asked in return.{p}
rows.10:57a0:
The skull vanished in an instant.
Before I knew it, the three who were left had gathered around {f:me|me}.
"What now? Three of 'em have vanished on us.
You still gonna keep this going?"
One of them asked.
What should I do?
I never dreamed it would come to this.
Maybe I could still turn back now.
If I kept on like this, I felt I'd only sink in deeper...
I couldn't shake that feeling.
Was what was happening around {f:me|me} right now real...
Or was it an illusion...{p}Should I really keep going like this{f:?|?}
rows.10:6994:
There was a student who could kill the animals in the school's animal hutch without batting an eye.
Each time, a teacher scolded him, but the lectures were all appeals to his feelings, so the scolding made no sense to him at all.
"Morikawa, don't you feel sorry for them?"
"Sorry about that."
To him, it felt like no more than breaking some school equipment.
"You eat meat and fish yourself, don't you? Then quit eating it."
He looked like he wanted to say something like that.
Even on his way home, if he came across a small animal within easy reach, he would torment it to death.{p}
rows.10:76f0:
"So it was you after all."
It was Nakayama.
"To think it really was killed..."
"It's not like that.
I thought you'd be sad if you found out it was dead..."
"Liar!"{p}What do you think Morikawa did then?
rows.10:7990:
Some time later, when he'd almost forgotten about it, Nakayama, who had been absent all that time, was waiting for Morikawa near his house.
"Long time no see."
"Nakayama..."
"Lately, I've started to understand how you feel.
Look..."{p}
rows.10:8174:
In the darkness, something like a cord was moving.
"Nakayama... you...!"
She was strangling his parents with a rope.
"Oh my, I said I'd tell you next time, but you just couldn't wait...?
You know, it's the best, killing people.
With animals, you were my senior, but now I'm the one ahead.
Oh, that's right.
To thank you, I'll teach you how to kill a person.
Heh heh, heh... heh..."
Morikawa tried to lunge at Nakayama.{p}
